title: Medical Office Replacement Sourcing
name: Medical Office Replacement Sourcing
metaTitle: Medical Office Replacement Sourcing in Oklahoma City, OK
metaDescription: Sourcing medical office replacement property in Oklahoma City for 1031 exchange investors, checked for building systems, tenant mix, and identification timing.

sections.html: A medical office building isn't a generic office deal wearing a stethoscope. Suite mechanicals, imaging power loads, and physician-group lease structure all behave differently than a standard tenant improvement, and if you're running your own portfolio you already know that. In Oklahoma City, sourcing a replacement medical office asset inside a 1031 exchange means matching the building to your relinquished property's basis and doing it fast enough to make the 45-day identification window. We treat that sourcing job the way you'd staff a facilities audit, checking the mechanical file before we let a listing sheet drive the decision.

sections.heading: Where Oklahoma City's Medical Office Corridors Actually Perform
sections.html:
Stabilized medical office tenancy in Oklahoma City clusters along the NW Expressway corridor, the John Kilpatrick Turnpike loop, and the south side near Norman, where physician groups follow patient population rather than downtown office rents. Edmond carries its own smaller medical corridor centered on outpatient surgery centers and specialty practices that lease longer terms than general office tenants typically sign.

We also watch satellite suites near the hospital campuses on the north and west sides of the metro, since those buildings tend to hold occupancy even when general office vacancy climbs elsewhere in Oklahoma City. Knowing which corridor a building sits in tells you more about renewal probability than the rent roll alone, and it's the first filter we apply before a property earns a closer look.

sections.heading: The Building-Systems Walkthrough Before It Makes Your List
sections.html:
Before a medical office property goes on your identification list, we walk it the way an operator would, not the way a broker markets it. That means checking the items that show up on a service log before they show up on a punch list:

  • HVAC zoning that matches individual suite build-outs, not a single rooftop unit serving every tenant
  • Backup power capacity for imaging equipment or minor procedure rooms
  • ADA-compliant corridor widths and restroom counts for patient traffic
  • Parking ratio checked against medical-use code, not general office code
  • Roof age, warranty status, and any deferred maintenance noted in service records
  • Tenant improvement allowance history and whether suites were built out at tenant cost or landlord cost

Any one of these items can change how you price a building relative to a comparable general office property, so we document each of them in writing before recommending a candidate for your list.

sections.heading: Reading a Physician Group Lease the Way You'd Read a Service Contract
sections.html:
Medical tenant leases carry quirks that don't show up until you read them like a service contract instead of a standard net lease. Physician group leases sometimes carry early-termination language tied to retirement or partnership buyouts, which changes your renewal assumption even if the rent looks solid on paper.

Suite buildout costs run higher than general office, so downtime between medical tenants costs more per vacant month than a comparable office suite in Oklahoma City would. We flag any co-tenancy language tied to a specific practice group, since losing an anchor physician can pull ancillary tenants along with them, and we look for holdover provisions that could leave you carrying a tenant past their stated term without a clean renewal in place.

sections.heading: Sourcing Fast Enough to Hit Your 45-Day Window
sections.html:
Medical office inventory in Oklahoma City turns over slowly, so we start sourcing candidates before your relinquished property even closes, working from your qualified intermediary's exchange agreement and basis target. We coordinate directly with your intermediary on timing so the identification you submit reflects properties we've already walked, not addresses pulled from a listing sheet the week the clock starts.

That coordination matters more with medical assets than with plain office space, since a building that looks fine from the parking lot can carry mechanical problems that only surface on a service walkthrough. We build in backup candidates from a second corridor as well, in case financing or title issues stall your first choice.

faqs.q: Does a medical office building need to be occupied to qualify as replacement property?
faqs.a: No. Like-kind treatment for real property held for investment doesn't require the replacement asset to carry a tenant on closing day, though vacancy changes your income assumptions and your lender's underwriting. We still walk vacant medical suites the same way, checking build-out condition and system capacity before it goes on your identification list, since an empty suite still has mechanicals worth verifying.

faqs.q: Can I identify a medical office building I haven't personally inspected yet?
faqs.a: You can identify it within your 45-day window based on our walkthrough and documentation, since the rule requires unambiguous description of the property rather than a personal site visit. We still recommend you see it before closing, and we build that visit into the timeline alongside your qualified intermediary's schedule so nothing gets rushed at the end.

faqs.q: What happens if a physician tenant's lease has a retirement-triggered termination clause?
faqs.a: We flag that clause before the building goes on your list, since it affects how you underwrite renewal probability and any related ancillary tenants sharing the suite. It doesn't disqualify a property from being like-kind replacement real estate, but it does change the operating assumptions and the price you should be willing to pay for the acquisition.

faqs.q: How does backup power for imaging equipment affect exchange timing?
faqs.a: It doesn't affect your 45-day or 180-day exchange clock directly, but it does affect diligence, since generator capacity and electrical service upgrades take longer to verify than a standard tenant improvement. We check that early in sourcing so it doesn't turn into a surprise during your closing window, and we get a written summary of capacity from the current owner's maintenance vendor where possible.

faqs.q: Should my CPA see the medical office lease structure before I close?
faqs.a: Yes. We send lease abstracts to your tax advisor alongside the building documentation so they can flag anything relevant to your basis carryover or depreciation schedule before closing, not after. Confirm the specific treatment with your own tax advisor or qualified intermediary before you finalize the purchase.
